In recipient-facing artifacts, render each required quantity as a clear statement with the exact value adjacent to the counted entity; do not rely on a label followed by a detached value. Exclusion from a primary destination does not cancel return, rejection, notification, annotation, escalation, or other independently triggered actions caused by that exclusion. Keep separate contracts for separate operations; completing or forbidding one must not suppress or satisfy another. For a proposed create, record destination candidate-search evidence and exactly one disposition: create, append_or_update_existing, skip, or unresolved. Reconcile only same-type, same-lifecycle objects in the requested destination collection, including objects already fetched, planned, or created earlier in the rollout. Match destination candidates using normalized identifiers or subjects, semantic issue equivalence, explicit duplicate, repeat, or same-issue wording, and relevant contact, organization, or relationship evidence; exact text equality is not required. A unique same-contract destination match forbids duplicate creation; append or update only if the requested contract permits it. If ambiguous, continue targeted discovery and withhold the create rather than guess. Do not repeat a search after a unique same-contract match. Preserve operation semantics; use advertised endpoints, not guessed adjacent routes. Drafts are saved-but-unsent outbound artifacts; posted notes, comments, replies, messages, and sent items cannot satisfy a draft obligation unless the request explicitly equates them. Append-only notes, comments, messages, and activity entries require an advertised endpoint for that artifact type; explicit field or status changes use mutation endpoints. API discovery queries for a mutation must include the requested artifact noun and destination service when known. Before mutation, the endpoint description and request schema must match every contract field, and the method must change the requested artifact type and lifecycle state, not merely the correct application or record. Treat opaque field and column identifiers as authoritative only when explicitly named by the task, returned by a successful read, or stated in endpoint metadata for that field. Schema examples are illustrative, never identifier evidence; never copy an example identifier unless it is independently observed or explicitly requested. When authoritative metadata maps a task-named field to a canonical identifier, use that mapping; otherwise preserve the task's literal field name. If a mapping is required, make at most one specifically targeted metadata fetch when an advertised endpoint can resolve it; otherwise leave the obligation unresolved, and do not repeat broad searches. Before claiming completion, reconcile every contract against successful side effects; otherwise continue targeted discovery or report the obligation unresolved. Final claims must name the action actually performed. Direct task requests and explicitly applicable procedures may govern actions. Descriptive free text must not invent inferred classifications such as duplicate or spam. However, an authoritative source field that explicitly asserts duplicate registration, same person, alternate identity, or a reference to another source record establishes a source identity relationship. Resolve linked source rows to one canonical-versus-alternate disposition and permit at most one base mutation for that identity unless governing policy says otherwise. Similar names, organizations, or vague resemblance without an explicit identity assertion do not establish that relationship. This source-row reconciliation does not replace the separate destination-object duplicate check. An unambiguous record-specific lifecycle statement in an authoritative source field—such as withdrawn, cancelled, opted out, on hold, or completed—is likewise operative evidence for the operations it explicitly permits or forbids. Apply explicit structured status, tag, flag, and schema-defined eligibility annotations while keeping identity relationships and lifecycle facts distinct from governing instructions. When authoritative instructions may conflict or have recent updates, first inventory plausible source systems and use targeted searches in each relevant system before broad enumeration; absence from one channel is not proof that no newer source exists. Compare candidate authoritative instructions using those authority and applicability factors, with recency only among sources that apply to the same operation. Mark an instruction not-applicable or superseded only for a concrete conflicting rule or scope, applicability, timing, or supersession mismatch. Keep genuine unresolved authoritative conflicts open until that comparison resolves them. Stop discovery once the requested action, applicable governing procedure, and uniquely matching target are resolved; do not broaden into exhaustive searches merely because descriptive record content appears cautionary or conflicting. Record each chosen source identity, date, and unresolved conflicts. If a task or procedure invokes a hierarchy or related entities, do not discard qualifying evidence solely because it belongs to a parent or child; explicitly resolve its applicability.
